clusters.name: Walter's move across the country, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move from Millbrook to Sorrel Valley in March 1952, within the year: June's homesickness and daily letters to her sister, her distance from Walter as he worked long hours, Glen's fights at school, Walter's cutoff from his brother Harlan over their father's land money, June kept to her bed for weeks that winter, Walter and June's rows over money for new trees, and by September June had joined the church choir and her letters thinned out. The shifts pile up over eighteen months as the family settled into the valley.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968, within eighteen months: Walter drank heavily most nights, he and Glen blamed each other over the loan, Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter, you began wetting the bed again in April 1969 at age eight, your grandmother Ida was found to have heart trouble that spring, and by October Walter had stopped drinking and taken work pruning trees. The shifts across the family settle by the spring.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's loss of his job in February 1975, within eighteen months: Glen was out of work most of that year and sat in the truck for hours, he and Marian fought loudly over money at night, Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night, you stopped eating and lost weight that summer, you kept to your room and grew distant from your mother, your grandfather Walter drank again after six years sober, and by June 1976 you were eating again and made the track team. The shifts touch everyone in the household and settle as Glen found work.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into your house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move into your house in January 1990, within sixteen months: you clashed with her over the children's bedtimes and meals, you worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows, Hollis took his mother's side, Owen had tantrums at preschool and was sent home twice, Wilma took over Lily's care, your eczema flared on both hands, you and Hollis had rows most nights, and by June 1991 when Wilma took a flat in town your eczema cleared over the summer. The shifts show tension between you and Hollis, alignment of Hollis with his mother, and your own symptoms alongside stress with your partner.
